gap: No result ChatGPT got states that GardePro's own US store sells the E5 2.0 for $63.99 today, not the $79.99 ChatGPT showed, alongside the A3S at $56.99 and the E5S, the model its maker titles 'Non-Cellular, Non-WiFi', at $69.99. It also doesn't state that Bushnell's own store lists the Core DS-4K at $179.95 and out of stock, against the $159.99 B&H price ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: Cam & Canopy (cited) gives prices dated 2026-11-14, but they are mostly Amazon and list prices. It has no price for the GardePro E5 2.0, E5S or A3S, so it doesn't price ChatGPT's own budget pick. It also tags all seven picks 'SD / Wi-Fi' without explaining that. TrailCamSetup gives price bands ('Under $50', 'Under $100'), not prices. Its only no-radio claim is for the E5S. Digital Camera World's Core S-4K review (cited) returned only its headline to my fetch, so I could not compare its price. None of the pages compares maker-store prices for the full set, and none notes that the DS-4K is out of stock at Bushnell.
decides: This confirms GardePro for the budget slot and makes the gap bigger: from GardePro directly, the E5 2.0 is $63.99, which is $16 below the card ChatGPT showed. A shopper who means 'no radio at all' should be steered to the E5S ($69.99, titled Non-WiFi on the maker page) or the A3S ($56.99). GardePro also sells a Wi-Fi sibling, the E5WF 2.0, and the E5 2.0 title doesn't say Non-WiFi. In the midrange, the Core S-4K is $149.95 at Bushnell and the DS-4K can't be bought there today. That leaves the Browning Strike Force Pro X 1080 ($139.99) and Strike Force Pro DCL Nano ($169.99, 4K dual-lens) as the in-stock alternatives at the maker. Our GardePro E8/E9 3.0 Pro and the Link 1.0 system only fit the third clarifying option, where the shopper wants photos sent remotely.
